title: Current-run control plane and durable delivery evidence
summary: Wire the existing settings, decomposition, dashboard, failure-routing, cleanup, telemetry, and CI primitives into one active-run control plane. Design decomposes before dynamic parallel lenses; every failure is typed before correction; Build proves test design and code quality; separately classified run artifacts survive cleanup; and CI executes one authoritative unsharded Python 3.12 suite.
decision: Keep loop.py as a thin composition root over existing owners, with one pinned active-run snapshot and the private RunStore as the sole mutable run authority. Add only narrow build-quality and durable-artifact adapters; create no second settings file, graph authority, lifecycle, test runner, or dashboard store.

current_state.summary: Typed settings, decomposition, graph, dashboard, failure, cleanup, telemetry, CI, and release components exist, but important production edges are missing. Current Design graph publication can be stale, lens routing did not prove actual workers, Build/CI can bypass typed failure admission, terminal metrics lack a complete production caller, host acknowledgement is discarded, CI repeats pytest subsets, and cleanup has no explicit durable artifact boundary. The prior wave took 24h58m09s while CI was about 13m10s, so lifecycle churn is the dominant problem.

alternatives.name: Thin composition root over incumbent owners
alternatives.description: Pin one settings/candidate/run snapshot, sequence existing producers, and require sealed receipts at public gates. Store durable evidence classes beneath one run-adjacent artifact root while RunStore retains lifecycle authority.

gains: Closes missing production edges without a rewrite
Keeps one settings and run authority
Makes dashboard, correction, telemetry, activity, and cleanup independently observable
costs: Touches high-fan-in lifecycle and CI boundaries
Needs public journeys before obsolete tests are removed
tradeoffs.revisit_when: A second repository or remote service must coordinate live policy across independent installations.

alternatives.name: Replace orchestration with a new service
alternatives.description: Move settings, graph, dispatch, telemetry, and cleanup into a daemon or remote service.

costs: Creates a second authority and availability domain
Requires broad migration and cross-host authentication
Increases delivery time without closing current reachability gaps
tradeoffs.revisit_when: The product explicitly requires centrally revoked multi-repository policy.

alternatives.name: Patch each helper at its nearest caller
alternatives.description: Add local calls without an active-run composition contract.

costs: Cannot prove ordering or current-run identity
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Only as a temporary migration adapter with sealed input and output bindings.

contracts.description: Sealed active-run graph projection shared by every renderer, binding run, requirement, stage, candidate, settings, source, revision, and publication.
Closed candidate-bound Build, Evaluate, or CI failure observation and classification; only exclusive product failures route to Fix.
Terminal measured-or-unavailable usage projection with evaluator attempt identities and no missing-to-zero coercion.
Run-adjacent dashboard, dependency-graph, telemetry, agent-activity, validation, cleanup, and Retro evidence classes protected from cleanup.
Zero-lens proof of focused static checks, selector collection/execution, consumer radius, semantic severed edges, applicable fixture co-change, and proportional-suite freshness.

acceptance_map.validation: Drive a fresh public loop into Design and prove delayed prior-run values cannot replace its graph.

acceptance_map.criterion: Automatic decomposition completes before dynamic Design lens selection and settings changes alter actual selection without source edits.
acceptance_map.design_element: Settings-bound sequence and DesignTeamPlan with a cap of sixteen justified quick workers.
acceptance_map.validation: Change only safe lens policy and prove decomposition precedes a changed actual worker set.

acceptance_map.criterion: Every failure has a complete typed record before repair; non-product and unknown failures cannot enter product Fix.
acceptance_map.design_element: One failure schema, typed Build/Evaluate/CI producers, and class-owned correction states.

acceptance_map.validation: Reject uncollectable or shape-only evidence and prove real consumer mutations before portfolio pruning.

acceptance_map.criterion: GitHub Actions runs one unsharded authoritative Python 3.12 suite plus only genuinely independent validations.

acceptance_map.criterion: Dashboard publications, graph and dependency evidence, telemetry, and every agent activity log are stored as separate durable artifact classes beside the run and survive every cleanup outcome.
acceptance_map.design_element: RunArtifactStore projection beside the private run, allowlisted class manifest, append-only activity references, evidence-before-cleanup, and explicit cleanup exclusion.

architecture.cleanup_rule: Seal evidence first; delete only exact owned temporary resources; never target the durable artifact root; verify artifact readability and zero leaks.
architecture.ci_rule: One unsharded Python 3.12 suite; parallelize only genuinely disjoint validations; no pseudo-test join.

progression: consumer radius and semantic severed edges
test_strategy.freshness: Reuse green only for matching candidate, changed files/tests, settings, selectors, runtime, environment, and outcome; fingerprints prove freshness, not correctness.

alerts: Block on stale or missing run/requirement/settings/graph/candidate/worker/publication/quality/classification/metrics/cleanup binding.
Block product Fix for non-product, mixed, or unknown failures.
Block cleanup if a target overlaps run artifacts or ownership is ambiguous.
Block clean Retro when usage is missing without attributable unavailable evidence.
Block release for arbitrary pytest shards or pseudo-test join receipts.

risks.risk: Composition root becomes another god module.
risks.mitigation: Policy and effects remain in typed owners; loop sequences immutable inputs and validates receipts.

risks.risk: Graph publication reopens mutable files or accepts delayed output.
risks.mitigation: Seal graph in snapshot and require expected-head publication CAS.

risks.risk: Sixteen becomes a lens fill target.
risks.mitigation: Every optional lens names an independently evidenced uncovered risk.

risks.risk: Failure labels are mistaken for classification.
risks.mitigation: Typed facts feed one classifier; unknown holds and candidate changes sever authority.
Adjudicate by current contract and semantic mutation; counts never authorize deletion.

risks.risk: Cleanup deletes evidence or user state.
risks.mitigation: Reserve-before-use, live identity checks, artifact-root exclusion, and no deletion on ambiguity.

risks.risk: Activity or Retro exports leak private data.
risks.mitigation: Private detail, minimized pseudonymous projections, allowlisted exports, and TTLs.
Keep one suite, only disjoint validations, and no join job.

failure_modes.recovery: Restart Design from a new snapshot; never reuse stale authority.

failure_modes.mode: A Design worker is missing or unbound.
failure_modes.recovery: Hold Design and dispatch only missing bound work.

failure_modes.mode: Dashboard is stale, degraded, or unacknowledged.
failure_modes.detection: Publication CAS or graph state is not ready.
failure_modes.recovery: Preserve rejected evidence, disable actions, and replay current snapshot.

failure_modes.detection: Failure record or candidate binding fails.
failure_modes.recovery: Hold and mutate neither product nor tests.

failure_modes.mode: A selector does not collect or edge proof is ceremonial.
failure_modes.detection: Build quality collection or semantic mutation fails.
failure_modes.recovery: Classify as test-design failure and rerun only the invalidated layer.

failure_modes.detection: Terminal metrics lacks measured provider receipt.
failure_modes.recovery: Emit attributable unavailable with null totals.

failure_modes.mode: Cleanup overlaps durable artifacts or ownership is ambiguous.
failure_modes.detection: Containment, identity, or exclusion check fails.
failure_modes.recovery: Delete nothing and emit manual-recovery evidence.
Hold cleanup/sign-off and reconcile from private receipts.

rollout.strategy: Pin active-run settings/candidate state; finish graph publication ordering and artifact/activity durability; wire failure producers and Build quality; create public journey tests; then remove obsolete tests and duplicate CI jobs. Run focused local validation once, one authoritative GitHub matrix, Engineering sign-off, terminal metrics, exact cleanup, minimized Retro ZIP, merge, bump, package, and install.
rollout.rollback: Revert the whole candidate while retaining new run artifacts read-only. Never accept stale graph authority, unclassified Fix, a second settings source, or deletion of evidence.

design_route.execution: one parallel quick wave followed by one consolidation

lens_evidence.evidence: The consolidated 16-lens review found reachability rather than missing-helper defects. This contract binds one incumbent-owner composition path, public journey validation, artifact preservation, class-owned corrections, and one terminal suite; all requested changes are Plan work.

visualization.reason: The snapshot fans into stages, dashboard, corrections, CI, artifacts, cleanup, and Retro; sequence and evidence boundaries benefit from a visual.
